newsitem.title: UK: British economy grows 1.0 pct in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: British economy grows 1.0 pct in first quarter.

text.p: Britain's economy rose one percent in the first quarter of 1997, above analysts' expectations, preliminary official figures showed on Friday.

Year-on-year growth was 3.0 percent, the highest growth rate since the first quarter of 1995. Analysts said the figures strengthened the case for an increase in interest rates soon after the May 1 election.
Official interest rates are at 6.0 percent and the Bank of England has been pressing for an increase for some months to choke off inflationary pressures in the economy.

"The figures demonstrate that the economy remained buoyant during the first quarter," said Philip Shaw, economist at Union Plc. "We had a slight acceleration in the pace of growth and they do provide another argument for a degree of overall policy restraint."
Government bonds fell after the robust data.
The next meeting between the finance minister and the central bank to discuss monetary policy takes place just six days after the election which the opposition Labour Party is tipped to win.
